guides.title: Run FastAPI for $0
guides.goal: Deploy a small Python API without managing a full server.
guides.recommendedPattern: Start with Cloud Run or Azure Container Apps for production-like container semantics; use Render/Koyeb/PythonAnywhere for simpler demos.
guides.watchFor: Cold starts, outbound bandwidth, database cost, container build/registry usage and idle-sleep behavior can sit outside the headline free quota.
guides.nextStep: Add Neon/Supabase for PostgreSQL, Upstash for Redis and R2/B2 for object storage.

guides.title: Get a real Linux VM for $0
guides.goal: SSH into a persistent Linux machine and control Docker, systemd, networking and storage yourself.
guides.recommendedPattern: Oracle is the more generous infrastructure lab; GCP e2-micro is the simpler tiny always-free VM reference.
guides.watchFor: Capacity, eligible regions, idle reclaim, disk/egress quotas and account verification matter more than the headline CPU/RAM number.
guides.nextStep: Install Docker, OpenTofu, k3s, a reverse proxy and GitHub Actions deployment.

guides.title: Host PostgreSQL for $0
guides.goal: Use a real hosted relational database without operating Postgres yourself.
guides.recommendedPattern: Use Neon for branching/serverless Postgres, Supabase when auth/storage/realtime matter, Aiven for a managed-service comparison, or local PostgreSQL for unrestricted learning.
guides.watchFor: Storage, compute hours, sleeping/pausing, connection limits, backups and egress differ significantly between plans.
guides.nextStep: Connect from FastAPI, dbt, Power BI or a small ELT pipeline.

guides.title: Use MongoDB for $0
guides.goal: Learn document databases or host a small document-backed API.
guides.recommendedPattern: Use Atlas when you want managed cloud behavior; use Community Server locally when you want full control and no hosted quota.
guides.watchFor: Atlas Free is deliberately small; local MongoDB shifts backup, security, upgrades and availability to you.
guides.nextStep: Use Atlas for app data and keep large analytical files in object storage rather than document collections.

guides.title: Add Redis / cache for $0
guides.goal: Add cache, sessions, rate limits or queue-like primitives to an app.
guides.recommendedPattern: Upstash is a good serverless cache reference; Aiven adds a broader managed-data comparison; Valkey locally removes hosted quotas.
guides.watchFor: Command quotas, bandwidth and persistence semantics matter more than raw MB for small free caches.
guides.nextStep: Put Redis between FastAPI and a database, then measure cache hit-rate and latency.

guides.title: Learn Spark / lakehouse for $0
guides.goal: Practice Spark, Delta/lakehouse concepts and distributed-style APIs without paying for a cluster.
guides.recommendedPattern: Use Databricks Free Edition for the managed lakehouse experience, local Spark for unrestricted runtime access, and Fabric Trial when you need the Microsoft platform context.
guides.watchFor: Free Databricks is serverless/fair-use and non-commercial; Colab/Kaggle are notebooks rather than durable Spark clusters; Fabric is a trial.
guides.nextStep: Benchmark the same PySpark/SQL transformation locally and in Databricks, then store the plan and runtime metadata.

guides.title: Learn Kafka / streaming for $0
guides.goal: Produce and consume event streams without starting with a paid managed cluster.
guides.recommendedPattern: Use Aiven for a managed Kafka reference and local Apache Kafka for unrestricted protocol/ops learning.
guides.watchFor: Managed free tiers are sandbox-sized; local Kafka requires you to operate brokers, storage, upgrades and observability.
guides.nextStep: Feed events into FastAPI/Flink/Spark Structured Streaming or your FOIL simulator.

guides.title: Store Parquet / objects for $0
guides.goal: Keep datasets, Parquet files, model artifacts and static assets in object storage.
guides.recommendedPattern: R2 is attractive when internet egress economics matter; B2 is a strong low-cost S3-compatible comparison; GCS teaches hyperscaler object storage; R2 Data Catalog adds an Iceberg path.
guides.watchFor: Separate storage GB-month, operation requests, catalog/compaction and egress. 'Free storage' rarely means every operation is free.
guides.nextStep: Query the same Parquet data with DuckDB, MotherDuck, BigQuery external tables or an Iceberg catalog.

guides.title: Practice cloud SQL / warehouse for $0
guides.goal: Run analytical SQL without paying for a persistent warehouse.
guides.recommendedPattern: BigQuery gives the clearest permanent serverless warehouse allowance; MotherDuck gives DuckDB-native cloud analytics; Oracle adds another managed SQL architecture; Snowflake remains a trial reference.
guides.watchFor: Do not mix always-free quotas with trial credits. Query bytes, compute hours, storage and result caching use different billing models.
guides.nextStep: Run the same TPC-H-style query and normalize by runtime, bytes scanned and actual billed unit.

guides.title: Learn Power BI / Fabric cheaply
guides.goal: Build semantic models and BI locally, then temporarily add Fabric cloud capabilities.
guides.recommendedPattern: Do model/report work locally with Power BI Desktop + DAX Studio + Tabular Editor; use Azure SQL free as a source; activate Fabric Trial only when you need OneLake, notebooks, Warehouse or Data Factory.
guides.watchFor: Power BI Desktop is local; sharing/collaboration/licensing is separate. Fabric is trial capacity, not a permanent free cloud tier.
guides.nextStep: Create one report from Azure SQL and one from a Fabric Lakehouse and compare the operational model.

guides.title: Build CI/CD for $0
guides.goal: Run tests, builds and deployments without buying a CI service.
guides.recommendedPattern: GitHub Actions is a strong default for public repositories; GitLab gives an integrated alternative; Codespaces is useful when you also need a disposable development environment.
guides.watchFor: Private-repo minute quotas, artifact storage, container registries and larger runners can become billable.
guides.nextStep: Use CI to test the benchmark app, build a container and deploy it to Cloud Run/Netlify/Vercel.

guides.title: Run Python notebooks for $0
guides.goal: Get a browser Python environment without setting up a local machine.
guides.recommendedPattern: Colab is convenient for ad-hoc Python/accelerator work, Kaggle is strong around datasets/competitions, Anaconda adds conda packaging, Databricks adds the lakehouse/Spark context.
guides.watchFor: Notebook sessions are ephemeral and compute/accelerator availability can be dynamic.
guides.nextStep: Keep datasets and code in Git/object storage so the notebook runtime can remain disposable.

guides.title: FOIL zero-cost infrastructure lab
guides.goal: Run a realistic FOIL wind/IoT data path with minimal recurring cloud spend.
guides.recommendedPattern: Oracle VM hosts the simulator/FastAPI and optional self-managed services; Aiven provides managed Kafka; Atlas stores operational documents; Grafana handles observability; R2 stores files; GitHub Actions deploys/tests.
guides.watchFor: Do not make Mongoku or the lab stack a second FOIL source of truth. Treat free hosted tiers as replaceable infrastructure and keep exports/configuration reproducible.
guides.nextStep: Add Databricks Free Edition or Fabric Trial only as downstream consumers for analytics exercises, not as FOIL authority.

guides.title: End-to-end data-engineering lab for $0
guides.goal: Practice ingest → transform → lake/warehouse → orchestration → BI using mostly permanent free resources.
guides.recommendedPattern: Use Databricks for Spark/lakehouse, dbt for SQL modeling, BigQuery/MotherDuck for alternative analytical engines, R2 for object data and GitHub Actions for CI.
guides.watchFor: These are intentionally heterogeneous tools. Use them to learn architectural trade-offs, not to pretend one production system should combine every free service.
guides.nextStep: Version one small dataset and run equivalent transformations through Spark SQL, dbt/BigQuery and DuckDB/MotherDuck.
